sec: Prolactin physiology, molecular forms and regulation

items.q: What is the most common clinically functioning secretory pituitary adenoma?
items.exp: Prolactinoma is the most common functioning pituitary adenoma, presenting predominantly as a microadenoma. (Book p941)

items.q: Match the pituitary adenoma type to its epidemiological ranking or presentation — 1) Alpha subunit of FSH secreting adenoma 2) Prolactinoma 3) GH secreting adenoma 4) ACTH secreting adenoma … A) Most common overall but clinically insignificant B) Most common functioning adenoma (microadenoma) C) Second most common functioning adenoma (acromegaly, macroadenoma) D) Third most common functioning adenoma (Cushing disease, micro > macro)
items.exp: Alpha subunit FSH adenomas are most common overall (silent); prolactinomas are most common functioning; GH adenomas are second; ACTH adenomas are third. (Book p941)

items.q: Human prolactin is a single-chain polypeptide composed of ___ amino acids.
items.exp: Prolactin is composed of 199 amino acids, whereas GH contains 191 amino acids. (Book p941)

items.q: Which molecular variant of circulating prolactin represents the monomeric bioactive form?
items.exp: Microprolactin (little prolactin, 23 kDa) is the biologically active form of prolactin. (Book p941)

items.q: Assess the statements regarding macroprolactin: I Macroprolactin is an inactive polymer complex assessed by gel filtration chromatography. II Macroprolactin induces profound galactorrhea and hypogonadism.
opts: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Macroprolactin is an inactive form assessed by gel filtration chromatography and does not cause clinical symptoms. (Book p941)

items.q: By which gestational week do lactotroph cells appear in the lateral anterior pituitary?
items.exp: Lactotroph cells produce prolactin in the lateral pituitary and appear by the 24th week of gestation. (Book p941)

items.q: Which tissue is NOT recognized as an extrapituitary site of prolactin production?
items.exp: Extrapituitary production of prolactin occurs in the CNS, placenta, and uterus, but not the adrenal cortex. (Book p941)

items.q: Prolactin exerts its cellular actions by binding to a transmembrane cytokine receptor that signals via the ___ pathway.
items.exp: Prolactin signals through the JAK/STAT cytokine pathway. (Book p941)

items.q: What prerequisite is required for prolactin to successfully induce and maintain lactation in breast tissue?
opts: Breast tissue already primed by estrogen and progesterone
Concurrent high pulsatile secretion of LH and FSH
items.exp: Prolactin induces and maintains lactation in a breast already primed by estrogen and progesterone. (Book p941)

items.q: Match the regulatory factor to its effect on prolactin secretion — 1) Estrogen 2) Thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH) 3) Dopamine (PRIF) 4) REM sleep … A) Stimulates prolactin release B) Stimulates prolactin release C) Inhibits prolactin release D) Stimulates prolactin release
items.exp: Estrogen, TRH, VIP, oxytocin, and REM sleep stimulate prolactin release; dopamine (PRIF) inhibits prolactin release. (Book p941)

items.q: A 26-year-old woman undergoes polysomnography. Prolactin secretion exhibits physiological episodic nocturnal surges correlated with:
opts: Awake state immediately prior to sleep
items.exp: Prolactin release is physiologically stimulated during REM sleep. (Book p941)

items.q: Identify the factor that does NOT stimulate prolactin release:
items.exp: Dopamine is the primary prolactin inhibitory factor (PRIF); TRH, VIP, and oxytocin stimulate release. (Book p941)

items.q: Assess the classification of pituitary adenomas by size: I Microadenomas measure less than or equal to 1 cm. II Macroadenomas measure greater than or equal to 1 cm.
opts: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Pituitary microadenomas are defined as <= 1 cm and macroadenomas as >= 1 cm. (Book p941)
